fr.recommendations:
• Mark the single access point with a visible address identifier readable from the approaching road.
• Post a site map near the access point showing the locations of all three structures, the drive aisle, and the service area.
• Keep the internal drive aisle clear of parked vehicles to allow emergency vehicles to reach all structures.
• Mark the dumpster enclosure location on any posted site map so responders can account for it during operations.
• Trim dense vegetation along the internal drive aisle to maintain clear sightlines between the access point and all structures.
• Keep the walkway between structures free of obstructions to allow responder movement on foot between buildings.
• Identify and mark any secondary or rear access paths to the main and detached buildings, even if informal, to give responders advance knowledge of available movement options.
• Where rear access to structures is blocked by vegetation, clear a defined path wide enough for responders on foot to reach the back of each building.
• Keep the service area clear of stored materials that could block vehicle positioning near the secondary or detached buildings.
• Label each structure with a visible identifier — such as Building A, B, and C — so responders can communicate locations clearly during an incident.

wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim shrubs and low-hanging tree branches that are in direct contact with or immediately adjacent to the building exterior.
• Remove dead or dry grass accumulations that have collected against the building foundation or along the base of exterior walls.
• Thin scattered shrubs located closest to the building to create clear separation between the plant material and the structure.
• Keep the large paved area and open terrain around the building free of dead leaves, dry grass clippings, and other loose plant material that can collect and ignite.
